prompt: Each team's dashboard is green, and checkout is still slow. What can show where the time goes?
hint: Something that follows one request across services.

choices.text: A higher-resolution metric on the API
choices.why: Finer API metrics still describe only the API.

choices.text: A trace, following one request through all three
choices.why: Right. It follows one request across every service it touches.

choices.text: Longer log retention in each service
choices.why: Keeping logs longer does not connect one service's lines to another's.

choices.text: A composite alarm over the three services
choices.why: It can say something is wrong, not where the time went.

prompt: Match each tracing term to what it is.
hint: From the whole journey down to one piece of it.

pairs.right: A timed piece inside a segment
The caller's subsegment a segment hangs from

prompt: A service in the middle of the checkout calls the next one without passing on `X-Amzn-Trace-Id`. What happens to the trace?
hint: The next service cannot know it is part of one.

choices.text: X-Ray joins the parts by timestamp
choices.why: Joining is by id; with no id there is nothing to join on.

choices.text: The whole request fails with a missing header error
choices.why: Tracing never fails a request; the trace is just incomplete.

choices.text: The load balancer adds the original id back
choices.why: A load balancer adds a header when missing, but a new one, not the lost one.

choices.text: It splits into two unrelated traces
choices.why: Right. The next service starts a new trace of its own.

prompt: In the lab's waterfall, which part took most of the 512 ms checkout?

choices.text: The card network
choices.why: Right. 420 of the 512 ms, two services away.

choices.text: orders-db
choices.why: The database answered in 27 ms.

choices.text: The API's own code
choices.why: The API spent most of its time waiting on the payments call.

choices.text: Sending the segments to X-Ray
choices.why: Sending happens after the request and is not in its timing.

prompt: moto reported a duration of 0.0 for a trace whose segment ran 512 ms. What should you trust?
hint: Separate what was stored from what was computed.

choices.text: The 0.0, since X-Ray computed it
choices.why: moto invented it; it computes no summary.

choices.text: The stored segment documents
choices.why: Right. They were stored and returned as sent; the summary was invented.

choices.text: Neither, since both came from moto
choices.why: The documents are the ones the program sent, returned unchanged.

choices.text: The response time of 1.0 seconds
choices.why: Also invented by moto.

prompt: A service's segment points at the caller's subsegment through its `___` field.
hint: Two words joined by an underscore.

prompt: Why does an X-Ray trace id carry the request's start time in it?
hint: Think of finding a trace among billions.

choices.text: So the trace expires exactly 30 days after it starts
choices.why: Retention does not need the id to carry the time.

choices.text: So two services agree on a clock
choices.why: Each segment carries its own start and end times.

choices.text: So X-Ray finds it by time, with no index
choices.why: Right. The id itself says when to look.

choices.text: To make the id human-readable
choices.why: Eight hex digits of seconds are hardly that.

prompt: With a reservoir of 1 per second and a rate of 5%, how many traces per second does a service at 200 requests a second record?
Why is the sampling decision made once, at the first service, and passed on?
hint: Think of a trace with holes.

choices.text: To save the other services the CPU
choices.why: The decision is cheap; completeness is the reason.

choices.text: Because only the first service may call X-Ray
choices.why: Every service sends its own segment.

choices.text: So each trace costs the same
choices.why: Cost is per trace whatever its length; that is not the reason.

choices.text: So a trace that is recorded comes back complete
choices.why: Right. Separate decisions would record the API and drop the payments service.

prompt: At a 5% rate, a rare checkout error happens 20 times in an hour. About how many of them leave a trace?
hint: Sampling does not know which requests will fail.

choices.text: About one
choices.why: Right. 5% of 20; errors are found by metrics and logs first.

choices.text: All 20, because errors are always traced
choices.why: The decision is made before the error happens.

choices.text: None, because errors are never sampled
choices.why: They are sampled like any request, at the same rate.

choices.text: About ten, half of them
choices.why: That would be a 50% rate.

prompt: X-Ray stores traces at 5 USD per million after 100,000 free ones. What does a month of 2,100,000 traces cost?
What does an OpenTelemetry collector do between a service and X-Ray?

choices.text: Decides which requests to sample
choices.why: Sampling is decided at the first service, in the SDK.

choices.text: Replaces the trace header between services
choices.why: Propagation happens in the services' requests; the collector sees spans after.

choices.text: Batches spans and exports them to X-Ray
choices.why: Right. Received over OTLP, batched, exported to X-Ray.

choices.text: Stores the traces for 30 days
choices.why: It forwards them; storage is the backend's.

prompt: Which header carries trace context in the W3C standard OpenTelemetry uses?

choices.text: X-Amzn-Trace-Id
choices.why: That is X-Ray's own header.

choices.text: X-Request-Id
choices.why: A common correlation header, but not the trace standard.

choices.text: Authorization
choices.why: That carries credentials, never trace context.

choices.text: traceparent
choices.why: Right. W3C Trace Context's header.

prompt: What does instrumenting with OpenTelemetry rather than the X-Ray SDKs give a team? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Changing tracing backend without touching every service
choices.why: Yes. It is a collector change.

choices.text: Traces that continue across languages and clouds
choices.why: Yes. One header everybody reads.

choices.text: Free storage of traces in X-Ray
choices.why: No. X-Ray bills stored traces the same way.

choices.text: No process to run beside the service
choices.why: No. The collector is one more process.

choices.text: Metrics and logs carrying the trace id
choices.why: Yes. The same SDK attaches it to all three.

prompt: Put the questions of a slow-checkout incident in the order the three signals answer them.
items: Is something wrong, and since when? (metrics)
Where in the chain is the time? (traces)
trap: Logs first is the slip: without knowing where, there is no log group to read.
